title: The unit along a finite surjective morphism is a monomorphism
statement: Let $\pi:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes which is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Then the unit $\eta_{\pi,G}:G\to\pi_*\pi^{-1}G$ of the adjunction $\pi^{-1}\dashv\pi_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is a monomorphism of $\Ab(Y_{\Et})$. (Intended proof, Stacks' argument: at a geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the stalk of $\pi_*\pi^{-1}G$ is $\prod_{\bar y'}(\pi^{-1}G)_{\bar y'}=\prod_{\bar y'}G_{\bar y}$ over the geometric points $\bar y'$ of $Y'$ with $\pi\circ\bar y'=\bar y$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction], and $\eta$ induces the diagonal map; the index set is nonempty because $Y'\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a nonempty finite $\Omega$-scheme ($\pi$ surjective) and $\Omega$ is algebraically closed; geometric stalks detect monomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono].)

source.place: Lemma 09ZE (label lemma-efface-cohomology-on-closed-by-finite-cover), proof, last paragraph (line ~14955: 'To see the desired injectivity we can look at stalks ... Since Y' -> Y is surjective and finite we see that the induced map on geometric points lifting x is surjective too'), with Proposition 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero) part (1). Stacks proves injectivity of f_*M -> f'_*M for f' = f o pi; this node is the same stalk argument for the unit along pi, from which Stacks' map is obtained by applying the left exact f_*. Reformulation by an agent.
